**Status:** Evidence-backed investigation. Exact syphilis-manager release
selection and digest verification are implemented; a model-consumer check before
promotion is proposed but not merged. A local [stage-1 likelihood check](#stage1-check)
passes with September's manager and reproduces the missing-outcome failure with
May's manager. This is not a check of all published versions or all locations.

**Verified against:** `jheem_analyses@16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3`,
the July 27, August 26, and September 9 syphilis-manager releases, and the
`codex/shield-manager-compatibility-gates` review branch at
`2bac62bcfcdeda516c92a45f1bf249c6a75d5505`. Release and workflow status
was rechecked on 2026-09-22. The dated probes below identify their own
source and artifact revisions.

The wider [reproducibility investigation](reproducibility.qmd) defines why
resolved manager identities belong in a run record. The
[HIV surveillance-manager CI investigation](hiv-surveillance-manager-ci.qmd)
covers assembling a different manager from released sections and auxiliary
inputs. Since 2026-09-27 that manager also loads through the GitHub Releases
route, so `release.tag` can select HIV builds as well as syphilis ones.

As of 2026-10-01, ordinary `latest` loading also resolves an immutable promoted
version and verifies its digest before loading
([`7f687a8a`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/7f687a8aa1e01080fa5626c82ed67f673fd9b705)).
The [loader documentation](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/7f687a8aa1e01080fa5626c82ed67f673fd9b705/commoncode/data-manager-releases.md)
describes version selection, offline migration, and corruption handling.
Changing an explicit selection does not move the shared promoted alias or the
local default pointer. Ordinary SHIELD requested the promoted manager on October
1, then pinned September 9 on October 2
([`38b20dcf`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/38b20dcfa1e879c46e5489b0a52ffa1045e91582));
the retained recorded pilot uses an explicit July 27 selection. The October 2
[loader hardening](#loader-hardening) stops failed online resolution instead of
substituting a cached input, and logs the loaded release and digest. The older
fallback behavior and its observed consequence are documented below.

## Manager compatibility and rollback

A manager can be internally consistent while being incompatible with a model that
consumes it. Changing an outcome's dimensions, source labels, ontology, location
coverage, or available years can leave the manager structurally valid but break a
specification, likelihood, or functional form. Manager validation and
model-manager compatibility are therefore separate gates.

### Reproduced SHIELD incompatibility (2026-09-09)

SHIELD names its runtime syphilis artifact `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER`. The bootstrap
loads `syphilis.manager.rdata`, not `surveillance.manager.rdata`, into that global.
The model's MSM initialization then makes two `proportion.msm` requests that
include `sex = "male"`: an Emory county request and a BRFSS state/race request.

At the time the failure was reported, `syphilis-manager-latest` resolved to
[`syphilis-manager-v2026.08.26`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/syphilis-manager-v2026.08.26),
SHA-256
`45446020e779f67ad58a0238ba8c505973dd9c8258d25caf84dd863033e2ace9`.
Its attached structural report already identifies the relevant regression:
Emory `proportion.msm` lost `year__location__sex`, while totals-level
`year__location` was added. Three sex-stratified BRFSS shapes also lost most state
locations. The build used the explicit force-update path and was subsequently
promoted to the approved alias.

A read-only probe against the exact release artifact reproduced the application
failure. For Baltimore, the current SHIELD Emory request returns `NULL`, which
triggers `Cannot get best-guess msm proportions`. The same request against
[`syphilis-manager-v2026.07.27`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/syphilis-manager-v2026.07.27),
SHA-256
`0d9bf7e02d58554a52844bdce85e0506c99aec27ac578d052f6b4d2eb89339eb`,
returns the expected seven-county array. That earlier artifact's structural
report records 687 checks passed and no failures.

Later on September 9,
[`jheem_analyses@cdd7ed7`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/cdd7ed7c84c045bba7ce9ffe9c5152e0debef8d9)
deliberately removed `sex` from the remaining national BRFSS
`proportion.msm` records and manager writes. The construction still calculates
MSM numerators over male-only denominators; totals-level describes the stored
dimensions, not an all-sex denominator. The resulting
[`syphilis-manager-v2026.09.09`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/syphilis-manager-v2026.09.09),
SHA-256
`c3e3c983d6b4e9c961f735f9c59d45483bd63cfa715cf75c1fae874da2d129e6`,
was promoted to `syphilis-manager-latest`. Its attached report records 698
structural checks passed, 3 failed, and 3 warnings; the failures are the three
removed BRFSS sex-stratified shapes. The structural baseline was force-updated
after the report was generated.

The September artifact returns `NULL` for both existing SHIELD MSM requests and
returns the expected Emory and BRFSS arrays when `sex` is omitted. A code-only
adjustment that removes `sex` completed `get.best.guess.msm.proportions()` for all
ten routine SHIELD MSAs. A second prototype prefers that totals-level query but
falls back to the earlier `sex = "male"` shape; it completed the same calculation
against the July, August, and September artifacts. The census population request
for 2010 also succeeded against the published August 26 census manager.

The reported 2010 issue is therefore not an independently reproduced missing-data
failure in this code path: `DEFAULT.POPULATION.YEARS` selects the census year,
while the two `proportion.msm` requests average their available years. This probe
establishes the totals-level shape as the intended current manager contract. It
does not establish numerical scientific equivalence: the derived SHIELD MSM
proportions are identical between the August and September artifacts for all ten
MSAs but differ materially from July. For Baltimore, the three race-level values
change from approximately `0.0493`, `0.0431`, and `0.0518` in July to `0.0331`,
`0.0316`, and `0.0366` in August and September. Those value changes remain a
domain-review question rather than an automatic consequence of accepting the new
storage dimensions.

The full compatibility path was then exercised locally with `jheem2@90b68ad`
installed as package version `1.12.3.9000`. For each manager version, a clean
runtime initializer loaded explicit manager artifacts into a temporary output
root; a Baltimore engine compiled, one deterministic median-parameter simulation
completed, and the stage-0 and stage-1 likelihood sets instantiated and returned
6 and 12 finite values respectively. This establishes executable compatibility
of the July, August, and September releases with the prototype adapter. The exact
September artifact also passed the ten-MSA contract and full Baltimore smoke. This
does not select backward compatibility policy, certify changed estimates, or
replace calibration-scale validation.

The immediate rollback contract should allow an operator or run configuration to
select a dated manager release and asset. A convenient alias may identify the
currently approved manager, but it must resolve to a dated tag and digest before
execution and that resolved identity must enter the run record. Failure of a new
candidate should not silently substitute an older manager: either the approved
alias remains on the prior version or the operator explicitly selects a known
version.

The corresponding promotion path is:

1. publish an immutable candidate manager with its digest;
2. run manager-internal structural validation;
3. run compatibility checks for the supported active models against pinned code
   revisions;
4. publish a readable compatibility result; and
5. move the approved alias only when the required checks pass.

The first model check can be deliberately narrow: resolve the candidate syphilis
manager and its surveillance/census dependencies by immutable tag and digest,
build the SHIELD specification and likelihoods, and evaluate a small calibration
path for a representative location in a temporary output root. Fast assertions
should first exercise the two MSM pulls, their ontology mappings, 2010 census
coverage, and all supported SHIELD locations. The end-to-end Baltimore smoke then
catches assumptions not visible in the schema contract. This gates promotion of
an approved manager alias, not ordinary source commits or the creation of
candidates. A forced structural-baseline update may still publish a review
candidate, but it must not by itself make that candidate eligible for promotion.

### Implementation status (2026-09-09)

Exact per-run syphilis-manager selection is implemented on `jheem_analyses`
`master` in
[`87fdd1d9`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/87fdd1d9604915536f399b3152464fafb3a62732).
Omitting the new final `release.tag` argument retains the existing promoted-manager
path. Supplying an immutable tag resolves that exact GitHub Release asset and its
published SHA-256 digest, materializes it under a version-specific cache path,
verifies the digest before loading, and attaches the resolved identity to the
loaded manager. Offline loading requires an already cached artifact whose metadata
and digest both validate; it does not contact GitHub or substitute another version.
The focused regression script covers legacy positional dispatch, exact and alias
resolution, concurrent cache access, corruption detection and repair, and digest
mismatch rejection. An end-to-end check also loaded the July 27 historical manager
through the public entry point and reloaded it offline.

SHIELD's bootstrap gained an opt-in selector in
[`11b70172`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/11b701726d74608e3c5fc2c20c3c9cb6d1bc6ac1).
A run can set `SYPHILIS.MANAGER.RELEASE.TAG` before sourcing the bootstrap or use
`JHEEM_SYPHILIS_MANAGER_TAG` in a batch environment. With neither set, SHIELD
continues to load the promoted manager. If a manager is already present, the
bootstrap preserves it and warns rather than pretending the requested selector
took effect. Repository-local usage documentation lives beside the loader in
`commoncode/data-manager-releases.md`.

At the September 9 review, an unmerged `jheem_analyses` proposal was four
upstream commits behind `master` and separated the work into two commits.
Commit
[`2bac62bc`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/2bac62bcfcdeda516c92a45f1bf249c6a75d5505),
published on the `codex/shield-manager-compatibility-gates` review branch,
implements the non-mutating runtime initializer, ten-MSA
contract, Baltimore smoke, and build/promotion gates described above without
changing the two SHIELD manager queries. The tests use the installed package
path; CI installs the exact requested `jheem2` revision. The promotion proposal
also requires explicit immutable census-manager and `jheem2` inputs and refuses
to move the approved alias unless the candidate's structural report and both
SHIELD checks pass. With unchanged application behavior, that commit rejects the
August 26 artifact in all ten MSAs and accepts July 27; July also passes the full
Baltimore smoke.

The review branch has not been merged or exercised in GitHub Actions. A second,
local-only commit (`42d5f1f5`) layers the dual-shape SHIELD adapter described
above on top. It was deliberately not published while the data and model changes
were being coordinated. The data-side change establishes the totals-level current
contract, but whether current SHIELD should also load July-era managers remains a
separate compatibility-policy choice. The shipped release selector supplies the
rollback mechanism without making that choice automatically or changing the
current MSM queries.

### Current SHIELD adapter (2026-09-22)

The preceding paragraphs describe the September 9 review state, not the current
application. In
[`8c3021ce`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/8c3021ce5e65dd3d6bcc8a8fbee44524f6da78f2),
SHIELD's `get.best.guess.msm.proportions()` gained both query shapes: it omits
`sex` for managers whose `last.modified.date` is on or after August 1, 2026,
and keeps `sex = "male"` for earlier managers. The current
[source bootstrap](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/applications/SHIELD/shield_source_code.R#L14-L20)
explicitly selects `syphilis-manager-v2026.07.27` in source. The selector still
provides the technical rollback mechanism, but SHIELD's active default is not
the promoted alias at this revision.

The date threshold is an implementation proxy for schema, not an explicit
schema/version contract. This pass verified the code path, not the behavior of
that current adapter against all three published manager artifacts or the
ten-MSA/Baltimore probes. Those checks should be rerun before making the
unmerged promotion gate authoritative. The earlier value differences remain a
separate scientific interpretation question.

### Observed legacy fallback (2026-10-01) {#observed-legacy-fallback}

A native SHIELD calibration log reports HTTP 401 when resolving
`syphilis-manager-latest`, followed by loading an unverified legacy
`cached/syphilis.manager.rdata`. A read-only audit found that file's SHA-256
matches the published
[`syphilis-manager-v2026.05.05`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/releases/tag/syphilis-manager-v2026.05.05)
asset exactly, not the promoted September 9 asset or the recorded container's
July 27 selection. The audited census file matches the container's August 26
release artifact. File metadata places both cached files before the run; this
is retrospective evidence, not a run-time input receipt.

This follows the
[ordinary loader's fallback](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/03e3eea538d862e84dfd22b3300d56c7ecf11d4c/commoncode/cache_manager.R#L533-L554):
after failed alias resolution it tries the last verified version, then permits
an unverified legacy file if no version pointer exists. The warnings expose the
substitution but do not stop sampling. The exact-tag path does not substitute
another release. At the audit checkpoint, this did not establish invalid
scientific results or the cause of the authentication failure. Confirm the
intended data with the model owner, preserve the active run's inputs, and
distinguish future-loading repairs from changes to an in-progress calibration.
Resolved input identities and explicit fallback policy remain necessary even when the application source
requests the promoted manager.

### Stage-1 failure and explicit selection (2026-10-02) {#stage1-fallback}

A subsequent operator report describes `calib.10.1.stage1` on SHIELD3 failing
because the fallback manager lacks `prop.male.ps.diag.among.msm`. The operator
identified an expired GitHub token and reported that replacing it resolved the
HTTP 401; September 9 was confirmed as the intended manager. This report is not
a separate file-digest audit of SHIELD3's old cache and does not establish that
it was the same May artifact identified above.

The source explains why stage 0 could finish before this failure: its likelihood
includes demographic terms and total primary/secondary diagnoses, whereas
[stage 1 adds the MSM diagnosis-proportion term](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/38b20dcfa1e879c46e5489b0a52ffa1045e91582/applications/SHIELD/shield_likelihoods.R#L710-L769).
Completing stage 0 does not show that its fitted data match September's manager.
Reuse of that predecessor requires an explicit decision based on its effective
inputs; changing credentials or the next stage's selection does not repair
earlier results.

Commit `38b20dcf` selects `syphilis-manager-v2026.09.09` for ordinary
SHIELD and removes the audited duplicate calibration registration. It does not
change the shared loader's online fallback behavior; the separate loader fix
below is now on master. The subsequent [October 3 check](#stage1-check) exercises
the actual stage-1 likelihood against the intended manager before a long run.
The container's two-stage operational canary uses stage-0
likelihoods in both stages and does not cover this missing outcome.

### Loader hardening landed (2026-10-02) {#loader-hardening}

The [loader on master](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/336df26d6e04f387b9ecfc655a26607b0b6491dc/commoncode/cache_manager.R)
retries an authenticated HTTP 401 once anonymously, for the same known-public
JHEEM manager release URL. Other repositories, endpoints, and HTTP failures do
not receive that retry. Release selection and digest verification still apply.
If online alias resolution ultimately fails, loading stops instead of selecting
a cached substitute; `offline=TRUE` remains an explicit choice. Exact-tag
selection remains available independently of the promoted alias.

[Linux and Windows tests](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/actions/runs/37040001420)
passed for the exact landed commit's mocked HTTP cases, cache behavior, identity
logging, and ordinary/recorded SHIELD selection. Both exact and promoted loads
now print the resolved tag and full SHA-256 only after successful loading;
verified offline loads report the same identity. SHIELD's editable ordinary
selection remains September 9, with recorded configuration taking precedence.
Startup wording distinguishes requesting a release from actually loading it.
This does not update server checkouts or any running calibration's manager.
The owning repository's
[loader reference](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/336df26d6e04f387b9ecfc655a26607b0b6491dc/commoncode/data-manager-releases.md)
documents the behavior and explicit offline option.

Release selection and failure handling are separate choices. The shared
loader can legitimately follow the promoted alias when `release.tag=NULL`;
that request must resolve and verify an identified release or fail. For a
long-running calibration, keep a dated selection fixed across stages rather
than resolving a moving alias separately at each launch. The SHIELD ordinary
September pin and recorded configuration both support fixed selection; banning
`NULL` in every consumer is not necessary to prevent online cache substitution.
Neither a pin nor successful loading proves scientific compatibility or makes
an earlier stage's results reusable after changing the data.

### Stage-1 compatibility check (2026-10-03) {#stage1-check}

A local check loaded the real SHIELD specification and
[calibration registry](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/4264842ce3fda9fbbc9c3e6717f958c11b5152ca/applications/SHIELD/shield_calib_register.R#L38-L46),
then instantiated the registered `calib.10.1.stage1` likelihood for Baltimore
(`C.12580`). The scientific source was analyses `4264842c`, with engine
`9578726b`, sampler `4e0d13e`, and R 4.4.2 on macOS. Engine loading used the
recorded bootstrap's `pkgload::load_all()` path, not the ordinary hand-sourced
native launcher or a container. Managers came from separate, digest-verified
offline cache entries; no shared cache or active calibration was changed.

| Syphilis release | Observed result |
|---|---|
| `syphilis-manager-v2026.09.09` | Passed at three fixed parameter vectors. Each produced 12 finite likelihood components, including the MSM diagnosis-proportion term. The component sum, optimized total, and ordinary consistency-checking total agreed. |
| `syphilis-manager-v2026.05.05` | Negative control failed while instantiating the likelihood: `prop.male.ps.diag.among.msm` is not a registered outcome. No simulation or MCMC was started. |

The vectors were the full model's prior medians and two diagnostic variations
scaling both global transmission rates by 0.9 or 1.1. These are neither posterior
samples nor changes to the model's priors. The September and May artifact
SHA-256 values were respectively
`c3e3c983d6b4e9c961f735f9c59d45483bd63cfa715cf75c1fae874da2d129e6`
and `e8acbeb758ae4af4e149a62ef78c862a114a2d55f43a0c4695f49d9a8a9fa0e6`.
Both checks used census `data-managers-v2026.08.26`, SHA-256
`f8c710684ccfdfb3a5c8e6f4b54caf0417ab67afb82b89ab3259c4b8151e1053`.

**Boundary:** this demonstrates compatibility at the tested location and
parameter settings, not scientific acceptance, full stage-0-to-stage-1 handoff,
same-seed replay, or native/container agreement. The May control reproduces the
reported failure but does not identify SHIELD3's old cached file. No likelihood
formula, calibration registration, or sampler behavior was changed. The reusable
check, helper tests, and execution guide landed on analyses master on October 3
in [`94ba7298`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/commit/94ba72984737d71ea9ca8ed102a8add58b48e6f2).
The subsequent [hosted comparison](shield-container-pilot.qmd#engine-loading-comparison)
also scored these fixed vectors with September's manager. This diagnostic is
available in the owning repository; it is not a required manager-promotion gate.
The next runtime comparison follows the
[repeatability plan](shield-container-pilot.qmd#repeatability-plan).

## Syphilis CI as a partial template

The [hosted merge workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/build-syphilis-manager.yml)
has completed builds from released section, raw-data, and dependency assets and
publishes versioned candidates. The separate
[promotion workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/promote-syphilis-manager.yml)
moves the friendly `latest` alias after an operator selects a version.
This build–candidate–promotion separation is useful for other managers.

The present gate is narrower than model compatibility. Structural validation
checks the manager's shape, while the computed data-quality report is
informational. Additions can update the spec automatically, a manual override
can regenerate it after failures, and promotion checks that the chosen release
exists rather than running an active-model smoke. Default section, raw-data,
and dependency tags are moving `latest` aliases; the `jheem2` default is
`dev`. The [section workflow](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/16eff985372fd65be46871bf164acb6eff14beb3/.github/workflows/build-syphilis-sections.yml)
had no recorded runs at this audit, and its optional handoff refers to a
self-hosted workflow file absent from the verified revision. These are reasons
to copy the boundary, not the workflow verbatim.

For the requested HIV increment, raw-to-section automation of syphilis is not
a prerequisite. A candidate assembled from identified prebuilt sections can
have a valid, explicit section-to-final claim while upstream lineage remains
a separately stated limitation. This refines the earlier sequencing in
[D-015](../decisions.qmd); see the later working
[decision](../decisions.qmd#d-020).

## Next verification and destination

Rerun the current SHIELD adapter against the July, August, and September
manager artifacts, including the ten-MSA and Baltimore checks. Resolve the
scientific interpretation of changed MSM values separately from accepting a
storage shape. Then reconcile the promotion-gate proposal with current SHIELD
before allowing it to move an approved alias. Keep an explicit older release
available for rollback without silently changing an in-progress run's input.

Loader code and tests, compatibility smokes, release metadata, and build or
promotion workflows belong in `jheem_analyses`. This page remains a
cross-repository investigation until the supported manager-consumer contract
and promotion gate live beside that code, have run through CI, and have a
documented operator path.
